newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta share prices lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta share prices lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta share prices were lower by the lunch break on Wednesday as investors led by local players continued to unload recent gains, particularly in medium and small-capitalised issues, brokers said.
Although the volume was small, profit taking in certain blue-chips such as Telkom, Semen Gresik and Astra International pushed down the index, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index was 3.25 points lower, at 695.15 points. Losers led gainers by 52 to 43, with 62 issues unchanged. Turn-over was estimated at 224 billion rupiah.

"The profit-taking mood was dominant on the party of local investors. Although potential gains in some medium and small caps remain high, they just encashed their recent gains," Harto, broker with Bhakti Investama, said.
An analyst with a European firm said the market was likely to move in a narrow-range in the afternoon session as no strong fresh leads were available in the market.
"Election fever receded after the polling was over last week. But it is still there as investors remain concerned over possible post-election trouble," the analyst said.
Brokers and the analyst said reports that Japan's Jakarta embassy received a second bomb threat in eight days on Wednesday had only a small impact on market sentiment.
"This is not the first time in the election period. So far it has only been a hoax," a local broker said, but adding the market was watching closely the outcome of a revote in Madura island.

On Wednesday, people in one district on the island off East Java began a revote after angry Moslems alleging vote-rigging burned ballot boxes from the Sampang district after last week's general elections.
Brokers also said trade and inflation figures announced on Wednesday did not have much impact on the market as they were within expectations.

The government said Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $243.3 million in March against $964.3 million in February, while the consumer price index rose 0.19 percent month-on-month in May, compared with an increase of 0.56 percent in April.
Newly-listed ceramics maker Intikeramik topped the active list, with 43 million shares traded. It was last traded at 925 rupiah against an initial offering price of 750 rupiah.
Property firm Surya Semesta Internusa was also active on strong market talk that an Indonesian conglomerate or a foreign investor might take a stake in the firm.
Company officials could not be reach for comment.
